NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution No. 2490 and proposed
  Resolution No. 2491, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing
  directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via
  teleconference.  There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Members of the public may
  participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 830 5351 5467 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 830 5351 5467, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  DECEMBER 14, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:05 pm remotely via teleconference, in accordance with
Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490 and proposed
Resolution 2491, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and social
distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN’s son David Zuckerman, and granddaughters Ruby and
Amber.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 4A-L AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF NOVEMBER & DECEMBER 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 64482 THROUGH 64576 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $891,010.70 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 110121 THROUGH
  110521; 120121 THROUGH 120321; IN THE AMOUNT OF $298,378.16 FOR
  A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $1,189,388.86 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF OCTOBER 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
DECEMBER 14, 2021
 D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF OCTOBER 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

E.  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL JOINT MEETING MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 9, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 9, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

  MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION 2491 TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO
  IMPLEMENT AND UTILIZE TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY
  PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO
  ASSEMBLY BILL 361.

5.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PRESENTATION TO OUTGOING MAYOR STEVE ZUCKERMAN

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN introduced the following dignitaries to make presentations
to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN:

  Assemblymember Al Muratsuchi thanked and recognized MAYOR ZUCKERMAN for
  his leadership and service to the community.

  On behalf of Senator Ben Allen, Olina Wibroe-Benson recognized MAYOR
  ZUCKERMAN for his many years of service and year as Mayor.

Certificates received from Supervisor Janice Hahn, the City of Palos Verdes Estates, the City
of Rolling Hills and the City of Rancho Palos Verdes were also shared.

COUNCIL MEMBERS STEGURA, SCHMITZ, and HUFF each thanked and recognized
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN for his many years of service to the community, and for his work as
Mayor over the last year.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
DECEMBER 14, 2021
 MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN thanked and recognized MAYOR ZUCKERMAN and briefly
highlighted his many accomplishments as Mayor over the last year.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN opened gifts presented to him by the City and by staff, and expressed
his appreciation for all of the recognitions.

6.  CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN nominated MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN to serve as the City’s
next Mayor, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

  FRANK ZERUNYAN APPOINTED MAYOR BY ACCLAMATION.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN nominated COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF to serves as the City’s next
MAYOR PRO TEM, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  BRITT HUFF APPOINTED MAYOR PRO TEM BY ACCLAMATION.

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Los Angeles County Sheriff Captain James Powers spoke regarding additional deputy patrol
and support during the holiday shopping season, and the past year’s reduced overall crime
rates.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL REPORT FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDED
  JUNE 30, 2021

  Recommendation: That the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates receive and
  file Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) for fiscal year ended June 30,
  2021.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a brief staff report (as per the agenda
material), and introduced Brianna Schultz from the City’s auditing firm Rogers, Anderson,
Malody & Scott, LLP (RAMS).

Ms. Schultz provided a brief overview of the City’s audit and the Annual Comprehensive
Financial Report.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL REPORT
  (ACFR) FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 2021.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PARK & ACTIVITIES  COMMISSION  ACTION  ITEM:  ROCKBLUFF  PLAY
  EQUIPMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a contract with Dave Bang and
  Associates in the amount of $137,254.80 utilizing 2021-22 fiscal year budgeted Park
  Facilities fees, for the purchase and installation of playground equipment and ADA
  enhancements at Rockbluff Park with contract final form approved by the City Attorney

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
DECEMBER 14, 2021
 Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the source of funding for the project would be
Park Facilities Fees budgeted for under the Capital Improvements fund, as well as additional
funds allocated for ADA enhancements, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that the park is expected to be completed in
approximately four months, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted that Bang and Associates have provided play equipment
for other playgrounds within the City that have been very well received by residents.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Public testimony was received from the Vice President of the Rollingwood HOA, Doug
Wickstrom.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE A CONTRACT WITH DAVE BANG AND ASSOCIATES IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $137,254.80 UTILIZING 2021-22 FISCAL YEAR BUDGETED
  PARK FACILITIES FEES, FOR THE PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF
  PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT AND ADA ENHANCEMENTS AT ROCKBLUFF
  PARK WITH CONTRACT FINAL FORM APPROVED BY THE CITY
  ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: SNOW DAY EVENT
  DISCUSSION

  Recommendation: That City Council approve a Snow Day event to be held on January
  29, 2022, during the morning hours in the amount of $5000.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Discussion ensued about the use of water for this event while the State is currently in a
drought, the amount of water to be used for the event, and the possibility of use for the
melting snow after the event.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that staff would explore the possibility of
reducing irrigation at that park location after the event while the snow melts.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE A SNOW DAY EVENT TO BE HELD ON JANUARY 29, 2022 AT
  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK, DURING THE MORNING HOURS IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $5000, WITH DIRECTION FOR STAFF TO CONSIDER THE LOCATION IN
  AN EFFORT TO REDUCE PARK WATER USE.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  THE ERNIE HOWLETT PARK PERIMETER PATHWAY PROJECT

  Recommendation: That City Council approve the proposed task order with Willdan in
